idiom_name: test-local struct implementing the trait (RefCell for interior mutability) or an FnMut closure
implementation_notes: A Rust test is a function, but a struct with an impl block can be declared inside it, so the shunt is a test-local type that implements the collaborator trait and records through &self into a RefCell-backed buffer -- the same shape the Rust Book uses for its mock messenger, and the one that lets the SUT hold a shared reference while the test still reads the recording afterwards. Where the seam is a callback parameter taking FnMut, a closure capturing an Rc<RefCell<Vec<_>>> replaces the local struct and keeps the double inside the test body. Neither form needs a crate; mockall is the escalation once expectations and call counts must be verified rather than recorded.
pitfalls: RefCell borrows are checked at runtime: holding a Ref or RefMut while the SUT calls back into the same cell panics, so keep the borrow guard inside the callback body and drop it before asserting.
Rc<RefCell<T>> is neither Send nor Sync, so a shunt for a SUT that spawns threads must use Arc<Mutex<T>> or an atomic counter instead.

A trait method taking &mut self cannot be recorded through a shared &self shunt without interior mutability, and a SUT that takes ownership (Box<dyn Listener>) requires the recording to be shared before the move.
